title: Finite shift span gives a linear recurrence
statement:
Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $(c_n)_{n\geq0}$ a sequence of elements of $K$. For $j\geq0$ let $R_j=(c_{j+s})_{s\geq0}\in K^{\mathbf Z_{\geq0}}$ be the $j$-th shifted sequence, and let $V\subseteq K^{\mathbf Z_{\geq0}}$ be the vector subspace [def-weil-sequence-subspace] spanned over $K$ by all $R_j$, $j\geq0$. If $V$ is finite-dimensional [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], then there are an integer $d$ with $1\leq d\leq\max(\dim_KV,1)$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension] and $a_0,\ldots,a_{d-1}\in K$ such that
$$
R_d+a_{d-1}R_{d-1}+\cdots+a_0R_0=0\quad\text{in }K^{\mathbf Z_{\geq0}};
$$
equivalently (reading coordinate $n$) $(c_n)$ satisfies the linear recurrence of order $d$ with coefficients $a_0,\ldots,a_{d-1}$ from the index $0$ on [def-weil-eventual-linear-recurrence].

source.place: ## Proof, second paragraph ('choose the least $d\geq1$ for which $R_0,\ldots,R_d$ are dependent'); the equivalence it serves is literature/milne-lectures-on-etale-cohomology_LEC.pdf, p. 157, Bourbaki's Exercise 3(a),(d), stated without proof

proof.text: Write $D=\dim_K V$. Each $R_j$ belongs to $V$ by the definition of $V$. If $D=0$, then $V=\{0\}$, so every $R_j=0$; taking $d=1$ and $a_0=0$ gives $R_1+a_0R_0=0$, and $1=\max(D,1)$. This handles the zero-dimensional case.

source.place: ## Proof, second paragraph: choose the least d≥1 for which R_0,…,R_d are dependent
## Proof, second paragraph: choose the least d≥1 for which R_0,…,R_d are dependent

proof.text: Because $R_0,\ldots,R_d$ are dependent, there are coefficients $b_0,\ldots,b_d\in K$, not all zero, with $\sum_{i=0}^d b_iR_i=0$. The coefficient $b_d$ is nonzero: otherwise the same relation would contradict the linear independence of $R_0,\ldots,R_{d-1}$. Divide by $b_d$ and set $a_i=b_i/b_d$ for $0\le i<d$. Then $R_d+a_{d-1}R_{d-1}+\cdots+a_0R_0=0$.

source.place: ## Proof, second paragraph: choose the least d≥1 for which R_0,…,R_d are dependent

proof.text: Evaluating this equality of sequences at coordinate $n\ge0$ gives $c_{n+d}+a_{d-1}c_{n+d-1}+\cdots+a_0c_n=0$ for every $n$. This is precisely the asserted recurrence from index $0$ on, hence also the stated eventual-recurrence formulation.
